question.text: Anita earns Rs. 10,00,000 per year and plans to retire at age 60. She is currently 33 years old. Assuming an inflation rate of 6% and a post-tax return of 8%, what is her approximate Human Life Value (HLV) using the workbook's PV-of-annuity discounting method?

answer.text: Approximately Rs. 2,09,95,702 (about Rs. 2.10 crore) using PV(rate = 1.89%, nper = 27, pmt = -10,00,000)
Rs. 3,10,50,000 (using inflation rate directly as discount rate)

explanation.text: The Logic: The HLV real discount rate = (1 + post-tax return)/(1 + inflation rate) - 1 = 1.08/1.06 - 1 ≈ 0.01887 (approximately 1.89%). With annual income of Rs. 10,00,000, Nper = 27 years (60 - 33), the workbook uses Excel's PV(rate, nper, pmt) function. PV(1.89%, 27, -10,00,000) ≈ Rs. 2,09,95,702, and PV at the unrounded 1.8868% rate ≈ Rs. 2,10,04,210 — i.e., about Rs. 2.10 crore. The Trap: Rs. 2,70,00,000 (income x years) would only be correct if inflation exactly equaled the return rate. Using the inflation rate directly as the discount rate, or using approximations, gives materially different and incorrect results. Note: Always use the exact real-rate formula (1 + r)/(1 + i) − 1 with the workbook's PV(rate, nper, pmt) approach rather than the additive approximation (r − i), which can drift by lakhs over long horizons.
